frozenIndicators.definition: Expenditure-inequality Gini from Lorenz curve. Zero is equality, one maximum inequality. Original2023 inequality booklet printed8/PDF8 defines scale and rising inequality. Not income or wealth Gini.

denominator.definition: Expenditure distribution across resident population; Lorenz cumulative population and expenditure shares, not a rate denominator

frozenIndicators.displayName: Real adjusted annual expenditure per capita
frozenIndicators.unit: thousand real PPP-adjusted rupiah per person per year
frozenIndicators.definition: Canonical expenditure candidate is annual real adjusted IPM per-capita expenditure. Yearbook: Pengeluaran Riil per Kapita (Ribu Rupiah/Orang/Tahun). Official methods booklet PDF10–11: annual Susenas expenditure made real at2012=100 then adjusted using Rao-method PPP and96 commodities (66food,30nonfood). Cell11.153 means11153 thousand rupiah/person/year, not11.153rupiah.

denominator.definition: Per resident; consumption divided by household members, annualised and adjusted; not household total or percent

frozenIndicators.displayName: Average Years of Schooling / RLS, ages 25+
frozenIndicators.definition: Mean years of formal education completed by residents aged 25 years and over. This IPM component represents accumulated educational attainment, not current enrollment, annual entrants, completion flows, or teaching quality.

denominator.definition: Resident population aged 25 years and over.

frozenIndicators.displayName: Expected Years of Schooling / HLS, age-7 entry expectation
frozenIndicators.definition: Expected years of schooling for a child starting at age 7 under current age-specific school participation. The source sums age-specific enrollment/population proportions and applies a boarding-school correction. It is an expectation, not attained years or a forecast guaranteed for an individual child.

denominator.definition: Age-specific resident populations from age 7 onward; synthetic expectation starting at age 7, not the mean observed schooling of all persons aged 7+.

frozenIndicators.displayName: Upper-secondary Net Enrollment Rate / APM, ages 16–18
frozenIndicators.definition: Percentage of resident persons aged 16–18 currently attending upper-secondary SMA/SMK/MA/equivalent, including Paket C, divided by resident persons aged 16–18. Both numerator and denominator are population-survey concepts; this is not school-location registered pupils divided by resident population.

denominator.definition: Resident population aged 16–18 years; upper-secondary official-age band. APM numerator uses that same age band; APK numerator includes enrolled residents of all ages.

frozenIndicators.definition: Household access to improved sanitation under common BPS national survey classification: swan-neck toilet, suitable excreta disposal, own/shared with specified households; rural pit disposal can qualify. Not safely managed fecal-sludge treatment.

denominator.definition: All resident private households in each kabupaten/kota, weighted by Susenas; not population or water-provider customers

frozenIndicators.definition: Common BPS improved-source household classification. Protected sources include piped, bore/pump, protected well/spring and rainwater. Bottled/refill drinking sources require qualifying protected cooking/bathing sources under current household definitions; not laboratory-confirmed safety.

denominator.definition: All resident private households in each kabupaten/kota, weighted by Susenas; not population or water-provider customers

frozenIndicators.definition: Current formula reconstructed from freshly inspected numerator and denominator. Public first-level preventive/promotive and individual-care supply.

candidates.unit: percent of measured children aged 0–59 months
candidates.denominator: Survey-weighted children age0–59 months with eligible height/age measurements; not all residents or a fixed administrative child registry.
candidates.definition: Height-for-age below-2 WHO z-scores, including severe stunting, among children0–59 months.
candidates.methodologyNotes: Current table4.14 has all27 regions and total stunting. Earlier launch table4.54 had22 regions and separate subclasses. Current methods permitSAE whereRSE>25%, response<70%, no secure fieldwork, or change>10% versus2023; table does not identify each district method. Fieldwork crosses into2025 but source reference remains2024.
candidates.comparabilityNotes: Age group and total-stunting construct match SKI2023; change fromSKI toSSGI, mixed direct/SAE estimation and cross-year fieldwork require explicit review. Not a proven year-on-year change or direct-only panel.
candidates.recommendation: Retain for human review before designing a new common-year model; do not replace the frozen 2023 input.
caveats: Direct versusSAE assignment is not labelled for each district; do not infer it from the five launch omissions.
Collection ranOctober2024–February2025; source calls the reference year2024.
Use published CIs; no CI/rank significance is reconstructed.

candidates.comparabilityNotes: Copying the published Wasting column would drop severe wasting and change the frozen construct. candidates.recommendation: Obtain the official below-2 total, or review an explicit severe+moderate bridge with source precision and uncertainty limits. Do not replace total SKI2023 wasting with moderate-only SSGI2024.
caveats: Numeric coverage27/27 is not construct compatibility.
Separate severe percentages and CIs exist in table4.14; confidence limits cannot be added to obtain a total CI.

conclusion.rationale: The audit verifies 15 of 18 frozen constructs with full 27-region 2024 coverage, including two explicitly caveated panels, and 11 of 18 for 2025. Neither year is a complete same-year replacement. The literal floor-area boundary changes in both years; published SSGI 2024 wasting excludes severe wasting, unlike the frozen total; exact same-year Puskesmas population denominators were not reproducibly retained. The 2025 IRBI headline series also changes baseline and hazard scope. These are source/construct constraints, not permission to mix years or redesign the frozen model. Newer observations and a defensible common-year model are different states. No 2026 full regional construct was verified. Keep the immutable 2023 baseline as the only complete CIVX model; this conclusion does not claim that newer data does not exist.
nextSteps: Request an official floor-area-per-person tabulation retaining the frozen <= 7.2 square metre boundary; do not relabel the published < 7.2 band.

Obtain official total wasting below -2 including severe cases, or review an explicit severe-plus-moderate bridge with rounding and uncertainty limitations; do not silently copy the moderate-only SSGI column.

Reproduce exact-person 2024 and 2025 resident-population tables from the health agency, pair each with its own year's main Puskesmas count, and retain both component records before admitting any rate.
Review SSGI survey continuity, October 2024-February 2025 fieldwork and region-specific direct versus SAE estimation; keep the published confidence intervals.
Confirm the 2024 IKLH table with the originating provincial/ministry agency, including the published zero water component and the Cirebon narrative/table discrepancy.
Verify a full regional 2025 APM panel, 2025 nutrition estimates and 2025 IKLH calculation vintage before reconsidering 2025. Treat the rebased IRBI 2025 series as a separate compatibility decision.
Human review must precede any second-model design. Do not generate new scores, alter normalization or weights, integrate contextual candidates, or modify the frontend in this audit.
